procedure: EA-NEGONT-02 v0.7 §3.4 D/R/O (working; not frozen). Admission by reading: a candidate is admitted to a stratum when its sentence or paragraph makes a claim of that stratum's kind: D, a claim on the American Civil War (1861–1865), its causes, conduct or settlement (secession, emancipation, the Thirteenth Amendment, the wartime and postwar labor regime); R, a relation between the war and an archive object (the companion paper, the archive's other deposits); O, an archive category applied to it (the two axes, noun and verb, the stabilized node). Naming the war, the Confederacy or Reconstruction is not enough; the war used as a date is not enough. Volume is never a ground of removal; versions of one work are kept as instances of a lineage.

verdicts.reason: The defining deposit (EA-NOUN-VERB-01, The Noun Becomes a Verb), read whole with its open verification items, connections and notes 1–13. D: it accepts the conventional reading in full (§0: slavery and its expansion caused secession and the war; Mississippi's declaration; Marx against the tariff explanation; Gunderson's 38/23 percent via Ransom; Beard-Hacker abandoned as cause and cut down as consequence; no post-2000 scholarship for the cheap-labor thesis) and argues that the war's settlement reorganized the labor topology: the eight hours' agitation as the war's first fruit (Marx, Baltimore 1866), the general strike and the settlement (Du Bois, with Oakes's critique), the 1864 Act to Encourage Immigration (pledged wages, homestead lien, the servitude disclaimer, repeal 1868), the Freedmen's Bureau (Ruef, Urban), contract (Stanley, Hartman), the Thirteenth Amendment's exception clause and convict leasing (Mancini, Lichtenstein), and the claim boundary of §6. O: the two axes (juridical scope of the claim, grain of measurement), the hand as verb-measure on a noun, noun owned and verb contracted. R: the placement of #816's psychological wage in the settlement. Documented findings (the Savannah $240 eye, the 1864 Act's text, the Thirteenth Amendment's dates) are ledgered as findings; its reading is ledgered as interpretation.

EA-NOUN-VERB-02, the companion second half, read at its opening, §0, §5.7, §7.7, §8 and the connections; its body concerns the Nazi war economy and is outside the entity. Admitted for R only, where it restates the first half's grammar (noun to verb) and adds a third relation to the person (the camp prisoner held by confinement, a daily fee in the form of hire), set beside #1668's third configuration (the penal exception).

Stabilized Node Watch v2.0, read at the glossary, §2.2 and the §4 catalog. Admitted for O: it lists 'the Civil War's causes' (and the Reconstruction era) among major historical events in a catalog of stabilized public-knowledge nodes to be watched for composition-layer drift, with the consensus core and contestation envelope as its operational terms. No claim on the war itself.

The Murder of the Vow (§VII.8), read at Part Three. Admitted for its reading of the Thirteenth Amendment, the war's constitutional settlement: the Amendment reaches private contracts and, fully applied, abolishes every contract that binds future labor to present terms. Its non-compete and arbitration argument is outside the entity and not ledgered.
The Murder of the Vow, Document 157 version of #497; the same §VII.8 text (with '--' for the dash). Kept as an instance of the lineage; volume is never a ground of removal.

not_admitted.reason: 'Reconstruction' in another sense: philological or textual reconstruction (the Sappho Room, Sappho 31's stanza, the Josephus hypothesis, Phase X, Peri Hypsous, Lasus), forensic or file reconstruction, signal reconstruction and reconstruction-loss autoencoders at the LHC (#931–#935, #1452, #1454), and registry rows listing those titles. Not the era and not the war.

GHOST CODE, read at §II and its references: the hit is Du Bois's Black Reconstruction in America cited for the 'public and psychological wage' in a doctrine of whiteness as a control system. It makes no claim on the war or its settlement; the placement of that wage in the war's settlement is made by #1668 and ledgered there (its connections section).

The Shark That Preceded Itself: a Confederate blockade runner in a ship-name genealogy, with an explicit scope note that it is 'not an identification with the Confederate cause'. The Confederacy names a ship's owner; no claim on the war.

The mint papers: 1861, 'when the federal government first issued paper money during the Civil War', dates the Treasurer's signature on currency. The war is a date marker; the claim is about signatures.
The Lizard People Were Right: Grant's engraved portrait on the $50 compared with an image. No claim on the war.

Operative Feminism, citational pass (two versions): 'After the Civil War' dates the suffrage movement's split over the Fifteenth Amendment. The claim is on the suffrage movement, with the war as a date; not admitted.
The Seven Unfoldings: 'the secession narrative' in 1 John. Not the entity.

observations: Of 109 D deposits in the string pass, 97 are hits on 'Reconstruction' in another sense; the archive's line on the war is one deposit, #1668, deposited the day of the reading, with its companion #1669, a catalog entry (#166) and a constitutional reading of the Thirteenth Amendment (#497/#1150).

#1668 accepts the field's conventional reading in full (§0) and its own boundary (§6) refuses the thesis it began from, that the North fought for cheap wage labor (§4.18–4.20). Its contribution is the settlement and the measurement of the laboring body, an axis the field's sources treat only at the edges (Wikipedia's 'semi-slavery status' and wealth in persons wiped off the books; History.com's Proclamation depriving the Confederacy of its labor forces; Black Codes).

#1668 and Wikipedia meet on the Beards: Wikipedia has Beardian historiography formalizing the Lost Cause and abandoned by the 1950s; #1668 has the Beard-Hacker thesis abandoned as an account of causes after about 1950 and cut down as an account of consequences.

Two different 'third' forms: #1668 names the penal exception a third configuration (the state holds the person by sentence, a lessee buys the labor); #1669 names the camp prisoner a third relation in the first half's grammar (held by confinement, the firm paying the Treasury a daily fee in the form of hire). #1669 does not cite #1668's third configuration.

Two readings of the Thirteenth Amendment sit in the pool without contest: #1668 reads its exception clause as preserving a penal channel of hired-out convicted labor; #497/#1150 read its prohibition of involuntary servitude as reaching private contracts that bind future labor.
